title: KV slab sharding for hybrid tensor/pipeline parallelism
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: KV cache memory consumption grows superlinearly for long-context workloads when combined with tensor and pipeline parallelism and continuous batching. Existing per-layer sharding designs cause many small cross-device transfers and complicate kernel scheduling for quantized paths. Goal: introduce a slab-based KV sharding layer that partitions KV tensors along the token axis into contiguous slabs owned by GPUs to reduce peak memory and simplify placement across hybrid parallel setups. The design must preserve correctness for causal attention, support incremental KV growth, and minimize latency regressions for short-context/interactive workloads.

decisions: Adopt slab sharding (contiguous KV blocks) partitioned by token axis across GPUs rather than per-layer sharding to simplify pipeline interactions.
Use per-GPU ownership bitmap and epoch counters to allow eventual-consistent KV syncs during pipeline parallel microbatches and to detect stale entries.
Expose slab size and sync window as runtime knobs; default to conservative slab size for hosted API and aggressive slabs for Dedicated long-context workloads.
Gate feature behind runtime.kv_shard_slab feature flag and staged rollout for runtime-1.20.
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces peak memory, simplifies global kernel memory planning, and groups transfers into fewer larger NVLink operations.
Cons: increases cross-GPU gather latency for short contexts, adds complexity for dynamic growth of KV during streaming generations, and requires careful handling of quantized alignment.
We favor memory savings for enterprise Dedicated customers with long-context usage; hosted default remains no-sharding to optimize single-request latency.
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype slab allocator and mapping layer (completed).
Integrate slab allocation into KV cache API and expose per-slab ownership metadata and epoch counters.
Implement NVLink-aware async gather/scatter with double-buffering and overlap with compute to hide transfer latency.
Add hybrid-parallel aware checkpoint/restore to handle slab placement changes during upgrade/rollback.
Add runtime feature flag, config knobs for slab_size, sync_window, and heuristics for choosing slab vs no-shard.
Rollout: internal canary -> dedicated customers opt-in -> broad enablement in runtime-1.20 after perf signoff.
tests: Unit: slab allocator invariants, ownership bitmap correctness, epoch wrap handling.
Integration: end-to-end generation with tensor+pipeline parallelism for 1K/8K/32K contexts across 2/4/8 GPU clusters.
Perf: throughput/latency sweep vs baseline, memory peak tracing and token-level cost breakdown.
Fault injection: simulate GPU removal mid-epoch and validate graceful fallback (recompute or fall back to host shard).
Regression: quantized kernel outputs must be within numerical tolerance compared to baseline (no sharding).
